audience.programmeDescription: Groningen Medicine studies the causes of disease and prepares students for medical practice through consultation training, supervised care and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore disease mechanisms, health behaviour and population health. Groningen combines these subjects with training and assessment in clinical practice.

cellNotes.text: Both study neoplasms and processes underlying disease. Groningen also covers endocrine and blood disorders in clinical context.
Both study pathogens, immune responses and infection. Groningen integrates those topics with medical cases.
Both cover disease mechanisms in the heart and lungs. Groningen also studies clinical presentations and care.
Both study brain function, including consciousness and cognitive processes. Groningen focuses on neurological presentations.
Both examine mood, anxiety and psychotic disorders. Groningen integrates the material with medical and psychiatric practice.
Groningen combines human development, metabolism and clinical cases in an integrated block.
Groningen introduces the systematic assessment of trauma patients.
Groningen uses longitudinal progress tests to assess medical knowledge.
Groningen trains students in medical consultation, professional practice, healthy ageing and research.
Groningen continues medical consultation and competency assessment, including applied work in a care setting.
Groningen students must develop an approved proposal before starting the bachelor project.
Groningen’s required project is part of this 20 EC block. The optional UCR research element sits outside the illustrated schedules.

notes.text: Groningen teaches medicine through biological science, clinical reasoning, medical consultation and supervised care. The UCR options explore related academic fields and do not lead to physician qualification.

The UCR options do not include supervised patient care, clinical examination and treatment training, or Groningen’s medical progress tests. Groningen’s required bachelor project is assessed within its final competency block.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.text: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

source.reviewNote: CP256: read the selected text and current course evidence in full. The concise cached description makes supported subject/method claims, with no unsupported disciplinary or project guarantee. Displayed text retained unchanged; source provenance recorded.

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.text: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

BENLEAD112.name: Leadership Communication
BENLEAD112.text: Studies leadership communication through theory, persuasion, emotional intelligence, gender, culture and ethics. Students analyse literary characters, film and speeches, interview a leader, prepare a communication advisory report, and develop an address explaining their own ethical leadership vision.

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.text: Examines how emotion regulation, emotional intelligence, belonging, identity safety and psychological safety shape leadership in diverse contexts, with particular attention to minority experiences. Students design and pilot a quantitative survey, collect data ethically, and use SPSS or RStudio for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlations, group comparisons and introductory multiple regression. They interpret the findings and develop evidence-based leadership recommendations.

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.text: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations. Case discussions and research-based frameworks address motivation, leadership, group dynamics, organisational culture, power, conflict and change.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.text: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

Students study utilitarianism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics, alongside Nietzsche, Murdoch and Nagel. HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease

Students connect anatomy and physiology with symptoms, disease mechanisms, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis across digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine and nervous systems. Students examine animal behaviour, research models, welfare and research ethics, then connect biological rhythms and regulatory behaviour to sleep, lifestyle drugs, mood and eating disorders.
